notes: PSA 4.8 ng/mL. PI-RADS 4. PSAD 0.07. Prostate volume 68 mL. DRE nodus. csPCa 0.80.

note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of rising PSA and PI-RADS 4 MRI finding following a previously negative biopsy.

Recently retired carpenter with a history of osteoarthritis and benign prostatic hyperplasia, currently managed with tamsulosin. He reports mild lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 0/35. The patient has been anxious about procedures and requested extra consult time. He is married, lives with his partner, and exercises by walking 45 minutes daily. He consumes 2 units of alcohol per week and is an ex-smoker (23 pack-years, quit in 2003). Recent appointments included thyroid screening with Endocrinology and cataract review with Ophthalmology.
Per rectum, a nodule is palpable in the prostate, consistent with clinical stage cT2a. The general examination is unremarkable, with normal vital signs and no signs of metastatic disease.

admin: Patient anxious about procedures — allocate extra consult time.
